title: 2018 AMC 12A Problem 9
statement: Which of the following describes the largest subset of values of \(y\) within the closed interval \([0, \pi]\) for which \[ \sin(x + y) \le \sin(x) + \sin(y) \] for every \(x\) between \(0\) and \(\pi,\) inclusive?

solutions.text:
For \(0 \le x \le \pi\) and \(0 \le y \le \pi\) we have \(\sin x \ge 0,\) \(\sin y \ge 0,\) \(\cos x \le 1,\) and \(\cos y \le 1.\) Hence \[ \begin{aligned} \sin(x+y) &= \sin x \cos y \\ &\quad {}+ \cos x \sin y \\ &\le \sin x + \sin y. \end{aligned} \] The inequality therefore holds for every \(y\) with \(0 \le y \le \pi.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: For \(x, y \in [0, \pi]\) both \(\sin x, \sin y \ge 0\) and \(\cos x, \cos y \le 1;\) compare term by term
